introduction: Find the hidden card table and the wandering priest, then choose among three independent item returns. Exact materials explain preparation; accepted exchanges keep separate histories.
orientation: Choose among three independent returns: three dark shadowy circles for Snarg, Threzik's exact pirate hat for Gisdan, or three lightning bolt charms for Shablem. Each accepted return has its own history; none requires completing another first.

Ask Snarg hi or hello, Gisdan hi, hello or yes, and Shablem hi or hello. These addressed replies explain their requests. Ambient gambling chatter does not record your conversation, a game result or another achievement.

From the main city, PUSH the rock near the hidden passage to reach the card table where Snarg and Gisdan wait. PUSH the tapestry on the table side to open the reverse passage. These are fixed controls; someone else may already have opened the passage.

The chamber also connects upward to the Shipyards wine cellar through a separate route whose secret door may need SEARCH and opening. Arriving by either route does not prove your own switch activation. Shablem starts in the city square and may wander.

Snarg wants three separate exact dark shadowy circles. Shadowclave supplies them on cloaked druids and named inhabitants; a cloaked visitor in Alatorin also has one. Bring all three loose. Supplied copies fit the request without proving that you personally killed a druid or recovered an item there.

Snarg pays 66666 experience and 66666 copper for all three circles together. Gisdan pays 25000 experience and 25000 copper for the pirate hat. Shablem pays 65000 experience and 40000 copper for all three charms together. These coins are rewards paid to you.

Threzik wears the exact pirate hat at the back of his den. It starts hidden; a successful SEARCH of the relevant corpse can reveal hidden loot after combat. His eyepatch and fireball wand are different items. Supplied hat proof also fits without recording your own search, kill or recovery.

The pirate hat has a no-rent flag. Its persistence depends on the actual item and accounting lifecycle; this journal does not promise an expiry timer or a particular rent outcome. Keep the visible exact hat loose when offering it.

Shablem wants three separate exact lightning bolt charms from the warlock lead at Thur'Gurax. Three orc warlocks at the Altar of Storms have one charm each. A charm starts hidden and may need a successful corpse SEARCH for personal recovery. Carry all three loose; merely reaching the altar does not complete the return.

The guildmaster's desk is closed, locked and trapped. Eligible lock-picking or knock magic can unlock it, but unlocking does not disarm its room-wide fire trap when opened. Its hidden ivory shard is a separate exploration lead, not an offering for these three quests.

The library bookcase starts open and holds a book and quill. Hidden coin sacks and other local treasure are separate exploration leads. Finding a coin sack is not a quest return; a committed wallet credit and a personal source history are different outcomes.

Gobo and Sulog have teacher data, while the goblin guildmaster and Maglo have teaching descriptions that need builder review. Paid skill practice is unavailable under active accounting. Local shop stock and training remain separate services rather than extra quest cards.

The underground ledge and pirate passages have falling hazards. Actual downward exit state, flight, levitation, climbing and mount state affect travel. The story journal does not require visiting every room or promise a safe crossing.

Every accepting giver departs after a successful return. A daily rollover does not recreate that giver, replenish an item or guarantee availability. Exact loose materials prepare a return; held or nested copies do not substitute loose offerings. Recorded history survives spent materials. All new discovery, encounter, journal, achievement and daily credit requires active, ready accounting.
